svg.title: DOGGO RAG Results and Decision
svg.desc: Figure 02. Accuracy of the First Pass, the Second Pass with retrieved notes and the Second Pass without notes for lfm2-vl-450m, qwen3-vl-2b and lfm3-vl-2b on 200 images; mean latency per stage; and the decision the evidence supports: lfm3-vl-2b First Pass only by default, lfm2-vl-450m with a no-notes Second Pass if memory is constrained, and no measured benefit from the RAG notes. Data: results/paired-summary.json and results/control/summary.json.
svg.text: Does a second look with retrieved notes help?
Accuracy, latency and the configuration the evidence supports.
Accuracy: First Pass vs. Second Pass
Images where both passes succeeded (failed outputs are not scored). 100 dogs, 100 look-alikes.
Mean seconds per image, model loading excluded. Full pipeline = Second Pass with notes.
For this task and these 200 images. Model sizes are the 4-bit MLX weight files.
First Pass wrong on only 6 of 200 images.
Faster and more accurate than every full pipeline.
A Second Pass adds +11.05% (21 fixed, 0 broken).
Closes over half the gap to lfm3: 88.4% vs. 97.0%.
About 4× smaller than lfm3: 0.38 GB vs. 1.59 GB.
qwen3 dingo accuracy: 22% with RAG, 67% without.
Keep the no-RAG control in every evaluation.
Retrieval must beat it before it earns a place.
qwen3 dingo accuracy, without → with RAG
qwen3: 78% First Pass, 67% without RAG, 22% with RAG.
